title: Bug: Everflow policer test can lose packets or hit ENOBUFS due to unpaced PTF traffic
author: zypgithub
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the bug

`EverflowPolicerTest` has two unpaced PTF traffic-generation paths that can overload the PTF data path and make the test fail for reasons unrelated to DUT policer behavior:

1. `checkOriginalFlow()` sends all 10,000 original-flow packets in one unpaced `send_packet(..., count=10000)` call. This can generate scheduler-driven microbursts and cause intermittent capture loss before policer validation starts.
2. `checkMirroredFlow()` first sends another unpaced 10,000-packet burst to absorb CBS, then continuously calls `send_packet()` in a tight loop for `send_time` (75 seconds on Mellanox). This can exhaust the PTF raw-socket/network transmit buffer and raise `OSError: [Errno 105] No buffer space available` before TX/RX PPS is calculated.

Both paths should use controlled pacing. The mirrored-flow rate must remain safely above the configured policer upper bound so the test still validates rate limiting.

### Steps to Reproduce

Run the Everflow policer cases repeatedly, including:

```text
TestEverflowV4IngressAclIngressMirror::test_everflow_dscp_with_policer[erspan_ipv4-cli-downstream-default]
TestEverflowV4IngressAclIngressMirror::test_everflow_dscp_with_policer[erspan_ipv4-cli-upstream-default]
```

The ENOBUFS failure was observed on `Mellanox-SN4700-O32` with `cir=100`, `cbs=100`, and `send_time=75`.

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Actual behavior in `checkOriginalFlow()`:

Passing captures peak at 52-57 packets per 10 ms, while failing captures spike to 119-192 packets per 10 ms and receive only 9,850-9,898 of 10,000 packets, causing the 99% assertion to fail.

Actual behavior in `checkMirroredFlow()`:

The unpaced 75-second send loop can terminate in the PTF raw-socket send path:

```text
File "/root/acstests/everflow_policer_test.py", line 312, in checkMirroredFlow
    testutils.send_packet(self, self.src_port, self.base_pkt)
...
File "/root/env-python3/lib/python3.11/site-packages/ptf/dataplane.py", line 180, in send
    return self.socket.send(packet)
OSError: [Errno 105] No buffer space available
```

When this happens, the test exits before logging `Sent ... packets`, `TX PPS`, or `RX PPS`, so it does not evaluate DUT policer behavior.

Expected behavior:

- Pace the 10,000-packet original-flow validation so all packets can be reliably captured while the offered rate remains above the policer rate.
- Pace both the CBS-absorption burst and sustained traffic in `checkMirroredFlow()` at a stable rate above `max_rx_pps`.
- Complete the full send interval and evaluate `tx_pps > max_rx_pps` and `min_rx_pps <= rx_pps <= max_rx_pps` without PTF packet loss or ENOBUFS.

### Relevant log output

```text
Recieved 10000 original packets
OSError: [Errno 105] No buffer space available
Ran 1 test in 76.398s
FAILED (errors=1)
```

### Output of `show version`

The failure was observed on `x86_64-mlnx_msn4700-r0` with HwSKU
`Mellanox-SN4700-O32`. 

### Attach files (if any)

No public attachment is available because the source report contains internal test infrastructure details.

linkedPullRequests.title: everflow: pace policer test traffic
linkedPullRequests.author: dlanov
linkedPullRequests.body:
### Description of PR

Summary:

Pace PTF traffic generation in `EverflowPolicerTest` to avoid unpaced bursts and sustained tight send loops that can cause packet loss or exhaust the PTF transmit path for reasons unrelated to DUT policer behavior.

`checkOriginalFlow()` previously sent all 10,000 packets in one unpaced `send_packet(..., count=10000)` call. This can produce short microbursts and intermittent packet loss before policer validation starts.

`checkMirroredFlow()` also had two unpaced traffic paths: the 10,000-packet CBS-absorption burst and the sustained send loop. The sustained tight loop can exhaust the PTF transmit path and raise `OSError: [Errno 105] No buffer space available` before TX/RX PPS validation completes.

This change:

- sends count-based traffic in batches of at most 60 packets with a 10 ms interval;
- uses the same pacing for the CBS-absorption burst;
- paces the duration-based mirrored traffic using `time.monotonic()`;
- preserves the exact transmitted packet count used for TX PPS calculation; and
- keeps the offered traffic rate safely above the configured policer upper bound.

The existing packet receive checks and policer assertions are unchanged.

Fixes #27708

### Test result

Local validation against master:

```text
python3 -m pytest --noconftest \
    --confcutdir=tests/common/unit_tests \
    tests/common/unit_tests/unit_test_everflow_policer_pacing.py -v

4 passed
```

Additional validation:

```text
python3 -m py_compile \
    ansible/roles/test/files/acstests/everflow_policer_test.py \
    tests/common/unit_tests/unit_test_everflow_policer_pacing.py

PASS
```

```text
pre-commit run --files \
    ansible/roles/test/files/acstests/everflow_policer_test.py \
    tests/common/unit_tests/unit_test_everflow_policer_pacing.py

All hooks passed
```

```text
git diff --check

PASS
```

No DUT test was performed. The local regression tests validate the pacing helpers and verify that `checkMirroredFlow()` uses both paced traffic-generation paths.

### Approach

#### What is the motivation for this PR?

Unpaced traffic generation in `EverflowPolicerTest` can make the test fail because of the PTF traffic-generation path rather than DUT policer behavior.

For the original flow, a single 10,000-packet send can create a short burst large enough to cause intermittent packet loss.

For the mirrored flow, both the CBS-absorption burst and sustained tight send loop were unpaced. The sustained loop can exhaust the transmit path and raise `ENOBUFS` before the test reaches its TX/RX PPS assertions.

#### How did you do it?

Added shared pacing helpers for count-based and duration-based traffic generation.

Count-based sends:

- send at most 60 packets per batch;
- wait 10 ms between batches;
- preserve the exact requested total packet count.

Duration-based sends:

- send traffic in 60-packet batches;
- pace batches at 10 ms intervals;
- use `time.monotonic()` for duration measurement;
- cap the final sleep to the remaining duration; and
- return the exact transmitted packet count for the existing TX PPS calculation.

The same pacing is used for:

- `checkOriginalFlow()`;
- the `checkMirroredFlow()` CBS-absorption send; and
- the sustained `checkMirroredFlow()` traffic.

The nominal pacing target is approximately 6,000 pps before send overhead, which remains many times above the policer rates exercised by the current test.

The following behavior is unchanged:

- `NUM_OF_TOTAL_PACKETS`;
- original-flow 99% receive assertion;
- policer min/max calculations;
- `tx_pps > max_rx_pps` validation;
- `min_rx_pps <= rx_pps <= max_rx_pps` validation;
- receive polling and packet matching; and
- platform-specific packet handling.

#### How did you verify/test it?

The unit tests use AST extraction so the standalone pacing logic can be tested without importing the PTF-dependent module.

Coverage verifies:

- 10,000 packets are split into 166 batches of 60 plus a final batch of 40;
- the exact packet total is preserved;
- 10 ms delays occur between count-based batches;
- no unnecessary delay occurs after the final count-based batch;
- exact-multiple packet counts are handled correctly;
- duration-based pacing terminates at the configured deadline using a deterministic fake clock;
- the final sleep is capped to the remaining duration;
- the returned TX packet count matches the generated traffic; and
- `checkMirroredFlow()` calls both pacing helpers and contains no direct unpaced `send_packet()` call in its outer traffic-generation path.

#### Any platform specific information?

No. This is a generic PTF traffic-generation reliability issue.

#### Supported testbed topology if it's a new test case?

N/A.

### Documentation

N/A.

comments.body:
The scope of #27708 has been expanded based on an additional failure signature from the same unpaced PTF traffic-generation pattern.

This PR currently fixes only `checkOriginalFlow()`. `checkMirroredFlow()` still has two unpaced sends:

```python
testutils.send_packet(self, self.src_port, self.base_pkt, count=self.NUM_OF_TOTAL_PACKETS)
...
while datetime.datetime.now() < end_time:
    testutils.send_packet(self, self.src_port, self.base_pkt)
```

On a Mellanox SN4700 run with `send_time=75`, the sustained loop failed before PPS validation with:

```text
File "/root/acstests/everflow_policer_test.py", line 312, in checkMirroredFlow
    testutils.send_packet(self, self.src_port, self.base_pkt)
...
OSError: [Errno 105] No buffer space available
```

Please extend the fix to pace both the CBS-absorption burst and sustained send loop in `checkMirroredFlow()`. The controlled transmit rate should remain safely above `max_rx_pps` so the policer assertion remains meaningful. Until that is included, this PR only partially fixes #27708.

comments.author: Xichen96
comments.body:
Validated the production pacing change on `testbed-bjw-can-720dt-1` (Arista-720DT-G48S4, M0) with tagged `SONiC.20260510.17`, build commit `dfb49be0fd`.

Pretest passed: 11 passed, 3 expected skips.

Same-bed A/B/A result for the exact downstream M0 L3 and upstream M0 VLAN policer scenarios:

- **A1, unpatched baseline:** 8 failures / 16 passes. Failures occurred in `checkOriginalFlow()` before mirror/policer validation, including zero-first-packet assertions and partial original-flow receives (`6555`, `7073`, `7437`, `6555`, `8011` of 10,000).
- **B, paced implementation:** 10 sequential iterations passed; **20/20 target cases passed**, zero failures/errors.
- **A2, reverted baseline:** 6 sequential iterations; 3 passed and 3 failed. Failing iterations received `7449`, `8104`, and `7808` original packets.

This same-bed fail/pass/fail control isolates PTF send pacing as the corrective mechanism; the failures occur before DUT policer-rate validation.

Validation interval: 2026-09-23 04:22-09:53 UTC / 14:22-19:53 Sydney. Final DUT health was clean: system state `running`, no failed systemd units, Monit checks healthy, and `gnmi`, `telemetry`, `swss`, and `syncd` running.

Evidence archive SHA-256: `509989693f24a1126301bb20a8015fa103ba0c4b5fc4029f975eb9d894200c92`.

The AST-based unit-test file was removed in commit `dd682b5b7e28097a68367b2166e771e0f7df9abd`; the PR now contains the focused production change only.

comments.author: Xichen96
comments.body:
**Design review notes / alternatives considered**

- We searched the sonic-mgmt repository for an existing reusable pacing helper. sFlow and VPP/KVM tests contain local count-based batching, while CoPP and DHCP stress tests contain duration/interval loops, but none provides the required fixed-count and duration-based callback semantics with exact accounting and immediate exception propagation.
- We considered extracting shared PTF utilities, but rejected that for this fix because it adds cross-directory import plumbing and unrelated scope. If another caller needs the same abstraction, that can be handled as a separate refactor.
- We considered updating sFlow in this PR, but rejected it as unrelated scope.
- We removed the AST-based unit-test file because it primarily tested source structure and scheduling arithmetic, not the real PTF failure mode. Same-bed A/B/A hardware validation provides the relevant regression evidence.
